synopsis: EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table), a mining-company group, supplies the PR-5A nine-level vehicle-interaction control model and mining scenario content; Level 7 covers operator awareness, Level 8 advisory controls, and Level 9 automatic slowing and stopping [f11736, f6229, f6750]. Effective Level 8–9 implementation depends on understanding the Level 1–7 baseline and integrating existing site controls: EMESRT guidance is not law or proof of mine acceptance, although South African requirements are framed at Level 9 and the relevant regulation was gazetted on 21 December 2022 [f11750, f704, f2586, f2587, f8233, f3624]. The corpus cites PR-5A Rev 3.0 dated September 2024, but other passages leave the current edition uncertain or say EMESRT was not reviewed or verified, so source verification remains a planning task [f6231, f4321, f9808, f11206]. EMESRT reports 17 surface storyboards published in 2019, while a trade article reports 24 scenarios; one chapter explains these as different measures, and the storyboards neither establish scenario frequencies nor cover hazards beyond those experts envisaged [f320, f7745, f6234, f6755, f6756]. A programme starting in October 2026 could realistically establish an operating-domain definition and scenario catalogue mapped to ISO 21815 and EMESRT by mid-2027, but no study applying OpenSCENARIO, ISO 34502 or the UNECE assessment method to off-road machines was found among the organizations searched [f831, f1698]. For mining acceptance, the booklet recommends combining EMESRT scenarios with MOSH numerical requirements, tracing the catalogue to hazards, and retaining assessor-selected physical confirmation runs covering every EMESRT scenario family rather than relying solely on simulation [f2645, f8030, f7887, f1122].
